findings.where: The address link in three places: on the first screen next to 'Write to me', in the footer, and set against the page's other links ('Replay the entrance', 'Download'). Desktop and phone.
findings.fault: The same email address is styled two different ways. Next to the button it is set in the grey serif with a faint grey underline. In the footer it is blue Public Sans with a blue underline. The palette swatch says blue is for 'Wordmark, links, the action', and every other link on the page is blue sans, so the most important link on the page is the one that doesn't look like the page's links.
findings.who_objects: A careful visitor, such as a bank officer weighing whether to write to Mark. They see one address looking like body text in one place and like a link in another, which makes a page that sells care look inconsistent. The founder would object too, since the page breaks the colour role its own palette section states.

findings.where: The two buttons: the filled 'Write to me' on the first screen and the outlined 'Download' pill in the article's document row. Desktop and phone.
findings.fault: The page's two buttons don't look like one family. 'Write to me' is a square-cornered filled block. 'Download' is a fully rounded pill with a thin blue outline and an icon. The rounded pill is the more eye-catching shape, but it goes on the minor action, while the page's main action gets the plain square one.
findings.who_objects: The founder, judging whether this direction could become a system. Two unrelated button shapes on one page read as parts from different kits, and that cuts against the 'well-set brief' restraint the direction promises.

findings.where: The photograph on the first screen (the exhibit) and its copy in the motion section, against the article's photograph. Desktop and phone.
findings.fault: The first-screen photograph has a wide, soft drop shadow at rest, as if it floats above the page or can be clicked, but it is a static image. The article's photograph sits flat with no shadow, so the page's two photographs are framed in two different ways.
findings.who_objects: Visitors, who may read the shadow as a clickable card and try it. The founder also, since the palette section says 'the photographs are the only material on the page': a floating-card shadow makes the photo look like a web widget, not an object laid on paper.

findings.where: Photo captions: under the first-screen photograph, and under the radio-interview photograph in the article specimen. Desktop most clearly.
findings.fault: The two captions are set differently. Under the first-screen photo, the italic serif title and the small sans 'Placeholder' note sit on separate lines with tight spacing. In the article, the two run together on one line, so serif and sans are mixed mid-line, and the sans note wraps with loose, body-text line spacing that leaves 'the image round.' floating below.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who will publish captions. The article specimen is meant to show her the pattern to follow, and it shows a different one from the homepage. The founder, judging the 'rhythm that holds when she adds an image and caption' that the brief asks for, sees the caption not holding.
